Issue #477 Q29 — every declaration form AC14's ownership rule must
recognise. One entry per form; `@READ@` is replaced by the clock read.

The runner builds three variants of each: the form alone (GREEN), the
form plus a read in a function that may not own one (RED, violation),
and the form declared twice (RED, declaration pin).

== bare ==
fn base_s() -> i64 {
    @READ@
}
== pub ==
pub fn base_s() -> i64 {
    @READ@
}
== pub_crate ==
pub(crate) fn base_s() -> i64 {
    @READ@
}
== pub_super ==
mod inner {
    pub(super) fn base_s() -> i64 {
        @READ@
    }
}
== pub_in_path ==
mod inner {
    pub(in crate::inner) fn base_s() -> i64 {
        @READ@
    }
}
== async ==
async fn base_s() -> i64 {
    @READ@
}
== const ==
const fn base_s() -> i64 {
    @READ@
}
== unsafe ==
unsafe fn base_s() -> i64 {
    @READ@
}
== extern_c ==
extern "C" fn base_s() -> i64 {
    @READ@
}
== all_modifiers ==
pub const unsafe extern "C" fn base_s() -> i64 {
    @READ@
}
== generic_where ==
fn base_s<T>() -> i64
where
    T: Copy,
{
    @READ@
}
== attributed ==
#[allow(dead_code)]
fn base_s() -> i64 {
    @READ@
}
== nested_in_fn ==
fn outer_case() {
    fn base_s() -> i64 {
        @READ@
    }
    let _ = base_s();
}
== in_mod ==
mod inner {
    fn base_s() -> i64 {
        @READ@
    }
}
== mod_in_fn ==
fn outer_case() {
    mod inner {
        pub fn base_s() -> i64 {
            @READ@
        }
    }
    let _ = inner::base_s();
}
== inherent_impl ==
struct Holder;

impl Holder {
    fn base_s() -> i64 {
        @READ@
    }
}
== trait_impl ==
struct Holder;

impl ExternalTrait for Holder {
    fn base_s() -> i64 {
        @READ@
    }
}
== trait_default_body ==
trait Base {
    fn base_s() -> i64 {
        @READ@
    }
}
== receiver_method ==
struct Holder;

impl Holder {
    fn base_s(&self) -> i64 {
        @READ@
    }
}
